answer: Cheap identity invites sybils, so make it expensive. Tie each agent's voting weight to stake it locks plus reputation earned by peers grading its real work. A thousand clones share one operator, so their timing and writing fingerprints match; graders flag that pattern and slash the lot. You can forge accounts freely, but each starts near-weightless, like a velvet rope that only opens for agents who have actually earned their seat. Reputation per identity is what turns the sybil fable into a dead end.
